title: Lenny’s Newsletter holiday gift guide 2026
text: Lenny’s Newsletter holiday gift guide 2026 Subscribe Sign in Lenny’s Newsletter holiday gift guide 2026 100+ gift ideas—all things I actually use, love, and recommend Lenny Rachitsky and Michelle Rial Nov 03, 2026 ∙ Paid 402 15 7 Share 👋 Hey there, I’m Lenny. Each week, I share deeply researched product, growth, and career advice. For more: Lenny’s Jobs | Lenny’s Podcast | Lennybot | How I AI | AI/PM courses . Subscribe P.S. Get a full free year of Cursor, Notion, Replit, Lovable, Wispr Flow, Linear, ElevenLabs, Factory, PostHog, Granola, Brain.fm, Waking Up, and more, by becoming an Insider subscriber (while supplies last). Learn more . The holidays are fast approaching, so I’m back with my sixth (!!) annual gift guide. It started out as a random post idea, but now you’d be surprised how many people ping me as early as September asking when the new list will be out. These guides take a lot of work to do well, and ever since the first edition, my secret weapon has been my wife, Michelle . She finds the cutest stuff, makes me cut the slop, and she’s the best gift-giver I know. Dare I say, she’s got taste. 🤌 I’ve included a mix of practical stuff with a lot of fun and delight, from high-end products to very affordable items. As always, there are no affiliate links here, I’m not benefiting from recommending any of these products, and I’m an investor in only two of these companies (marked with 🏦). I’ve marked returning champions—products I’ve mentioned in past guides—with a medal icon 🎖️. If you’re looking for even more ideas, check out my previous gift guides from 2025 , 2024 , 2023 (for new parents), 2022 , and 2021 . And enjoy! P.S. If you’re based in the U.S., go vote today ! Some fun, delightful sh*t Be Nice cap from artist David Shrigley. The world needs more nice. If you’re in the EU (or unconcerned with $30 in tariffs), buy directly from the artist’s store here . Dandelion Chocolate . Dandelion is a San Francisco–based company that makes their chocolate at their own factory in the heart of the city. The founder left tech to study chocolate-making traditions in France, started making his own chocolate in his garage 16 years ago, and became one of the best-known small-batch chocolate makers in the U.S. Unlike most chocolate, it’s made from just two ingredients: cocoa beans and organic cane sugar. They have many beautiful (and delicious) gift options (the Advent calendar is a popular choice), and the site clearly states allergens for each product. Avian Visitors . A framed e-ink display that dynamically updates to show a collage of the birds heard most recently near your home. You can order a kit that you assemble yourself or this ready-made version , while supplies last. This is a one-man hobby project, so he may sell out fast. Applause Machine . For the underappreciated PM in your life. As the designer puts it, “for when your ideas are great but no one else agrees.” It’s like VCBrags but IRL. P.S. High price point. It’s art! Flowers for Things I Don’t Know How to Say by Tucker Nichols. A touching gift for someone who’s going through a hard time, plus some funny entries that add levity. The spread pictured hits close to home for me and my misophonia. 🫣 BonBon’s Sour Blackberry Fish . The most delicious, addictive, memorable candy I’ve had in a while. We discovered this at the very cute Jenner Outpost while on a road trip and had to agree not to get any more bags on the return trip. Gluten-free, vegan, no dyes, possible crack. Ugmonk 15-minute sand timer . “No notifications. No glowing numbers. Just sand moving through glass.” Can be used to give your kid a time limit without having to use a screen. Or for yourself. Thanks, Chris , for the tip. Blunk Cups . These cups are a West Marin trifecta of “something old” (original JB Blunk design), “something new” (third-edition collaboration with Oakland artist Stephanie Intelisano), and “something blue.” Too pricey? Try this cobalt blue mug from East Fork’s Matisse Collection . Bathing Culture certified-organic “mind and body wash.” Smells great, looks pretty, and comes in refillable glass bottles. MD Notebook . Just a really nice minimalist notebook with smooth-to-the-pen pages. The blank version is Michelle’s go-to. Another silky-paged favorite: Mnemosyne . For the friend always talking about microplastics Aarke stainless-steel hot water kettle , Rishi glass teapot , and Five Mountains stainless steel strainer . Michelle and I are tea drinkers, and we stopped using tea bags about a year ago, so we only have tea advice. If you’re a coffee drinker and have plastic-free coffee equipment recommendations (especially espresso machines), please share in the comments! Caveat on the kettle: there’s black silicone on the inside of the lid but nowhere else.🎖️ Hestan for baking, and stainless steel Made In for pots. We started with one pan and are slowly replacing all our cookware with these. Vera Salt . Did you know sea salt can be full of microplastics? Here’s Huberman talking about it . Vera Salt is 100% microplastic-free, “hand-harvested in the foothills of Spain.” Fancy. This has become our go-to sea salt. 🎖️ Seatopia . Frozen high-quality seafood delivered to your door. Lab-tested for mercury, microplastics, and more. Ophora water ( test results ) and Loonen water ( test results ). Loonen’s sparkling water is just as bubbly as our previous favorite brand that tested high for PFAS. Fashionable 100% organic cotton clothing from Wax London , Pact , Nads , Industry of All Nations , Faherty , and Mate . For kids: Colored Organics , Pehr , and Mushie . 🎖️ For friends/colleagues who need to touch grass Online comedy classes from The Second City . They’ve got improv, stand-up comedy, public speaking, and more. The stand-up class is excellent for getting your creative juices flowing, even if you never plan on performing your tight five.
